info.title: AjBoilerplate API
info.description: Every response is wrapped in the ApiResponse<T> envelope — see ADR-0005.

post.summary:
Record how one session ended. Idempotent on the session: the first event for it wins, every
            other is answered `duplicate`.

get.summary:
Sessions, newest sign-in first, 20 per page. `userId` filters to one person; `from` (inclusive)
and `to` (exclusive) bound the sign-in time. `sortBy` is one of `signedIn`, `user`,
`sessionEnded`, `duration`, `result`, `endReason` and sorts across ALL pages;
`sortDir` is `asc` or `desc` (sortBy alone: ascending). An open session has no ending or
duration: SQL Server orders that NULL first ascending, last descending. Any unknown value is a 400.
The people the history names, once each and A–Z, for the User filter.

Active announcements the current user has not acknowledged yet whose page list matches
path — or whose page list is empty, which matches every route. Returns an
empty array when there is nothing to show.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description:
The path the client is currently on, e.g. `/reports/monthly`. Any query string or
fragment is ignored, and `.`/`..` segments are resolved before matching, so a path
is always compared as it actually resolves. Defaults to `/` when omitted.

post.summary:
Marks one or more announcements as seen by the current user. Idempotent — already-acknowledged
ids are silently skipped, so dismissing twice is a success, not a conflict. Call it on every
close path (the confirm button, the close icon, Escape).

requestBody.description: The ids to acknowledge. An empty array is an accepted no-op.

get.summary:
List items, newest first, optionally filtered by a case-insensitive substring of
            name or description.

post.summary:
Create an item. Returns 201 with a `Location` header pointing at the new
            resource.

get.summary: Get a single item by id.

put.summary:
Replace an item's name, description, and status. `rowVersion` must be the token from the
caller's last read; a stale one is rejected with 409 rather than silently overwriting whatever
someone else saved in the meantime.

delete.summary: Delete an item. 204 on success, 404 when no item has that id.

get.summary:
The current caller's identity, roles, and capabilities. Everything is derived from the
authenticated principal; no field is influenced by anything the client sends.
The portals the caller may open, in the order they are configured.

Search the directory by name or e-mail. A blank `q` answers an empty list without asking
            upstream. `limit` 1–100, default 25.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The search term. It is personal data: sent to the Auth service as a query string, never logged.

post.summary: Give a person a seat, creating their account when the directory has none.

get.summary:
Everyone who holds a seat in a portal the Auth service manages, with those seats. A portal whose
            `outcome` is not `Success` is missing from `members`; that is not "nobody holds a seat".
The seat groups the Auth service manages — the values `PUT …/groups` accepts.

put.summary:
Replace the groups one person holds. Send the full set; an empty array removes every seat. The
            response says what was added and removed. A failure can still have changed something (the Auth service
            adds before it removes and rolls nothing back): re-read the groups after any failure.

post.summary: Disable the account and end its sessions.

Flag every live session of the person for a re-exchange, so a changed seat applies without
            waiting for the next token renewal.

featureIds.description:
The announcements to mark as seen — normally every id the last lookup returned, sent in one
request when the user closes the popup. Idempotent: ids already acknowledged are silently
skipped, and an empty array is an accepted no-op.

AuthBackendSessionEndedRequest.description:
The Auth service's session-ended event (`docs/auth/session-ended-contract.md`). Every property is
nullable on purpose: a missing field must reach the receiver's own rules, which decide what is a 400,
instead of being refused by model binding — a 400 makes the sender abandon the event for good.

AuthBackendSessionEndedResponse.description:
The receiver's answer, sent BARE — not in the `ApiResponse` envelope — because the sender
            reads `outcome` at the top level of the body. `outcome` is `recorded`, `duplicate` or
            `ignored-unknown-session`.

userId.description: The identity provider's subject; the value to send as `userId`.

userDisplayName.description: A name recorded for them; null when none ever was.

AuthenticationHistoryUserResponse.description: A person the history names, for the User filter.

id.description: The row's id. Not the gateway session id, which is never sent.

userDisplayName.description: The name on the token when they signed in; null when it had none.

signedInAtUtc.description: When the gateway says the session began.

endedAtUtc.description: When the session ended; null while it is open.

endReasonDetail.description: Which check decided the ending (`idle_timeout`, …), for investigation; null when unknown.

result.description: `Failure` when the system signed the person out, otherwise `Success`.

durationSeconds.description: Sign-in to ending, whole seconds; null while open.

AuthenticationSessionResponse.description:
One sign-in session in Administration → Sign-in history. One row per session: its ending, when
            there is one, is on the same row.

AuthenticationSessionResponsePagedRespon.description:
A single page of results. Total is the full count across all pages so a
client can render paging controls; Items is only the current page.

CreateDirectoryUserRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/admin/users`: give a person a seat, creating the account when the directory
            has none. `Email` and `GroupPath` are required.

DirectoryGroupResponse.description: A seat group the Auth service manages. `Path` is what `PUT …/groups` takes.

DirectoryUserResponse.description: A person in the identity directory, as the Auth service reports them.

DirectoryUsersResponse.description: Result of `GET /api/v1/admin/users?q=`. A blank `q` answers an empty list.

id.description: Send this back to `POST /api/v1/features/ack` to dismiss it.

key.description: Stable machine identifier, e.g. `search-v2`. Not for display.

titleAr.description: Arabic title; null means "fall back to the English title".

bodyAr.description: Arabic body; null means "fall back to the English body".

displayOrder.description: Presentation order when several are pending; lower shows first.

createdAt.description: When the announcement was created, UTC.

FeatureAnnouncementResponse.description:
A "what's new" announcement the current user has not dismissed yet. The only shape that crosses
the API boundary for announcements; the EF entity is never serialised.

description.description: Optional free text, up to 2000 characters.

createdAt.description: When the item was created, UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the item was last modified, UTC; null if never modified.

rowVersion.description:
Base64 optimistic-concurrency token. Send it back verbatim on update;
            a stale value is rejected with 409.

ItemResponse.description:
SAMPLE SLICE DTOs — delete or rename alongside the rest of the `Item` sample.
            
These are the only shapes that cross the API boundary for items; the EF entity is never bound to
a request or serialized into a response.

ItemResponsePagedResponse.description:
A single page of results. Total is the full count across all pages so a
client can render paging controls; Items is only the current page.

portalKeys.description:
The key of every portal listed in Portals, for a client that
            only needs to know locked from unlocked. Same field name USP-Core's response uses.

portals.description: The portals this caller may open.

MePortalsResponse.description:
The portals the signed-in person may open — `GET /api/v1/me/portals`. Derived from the caller's own
capabilities and the configured portal list; the request carries nothing, so there is nothing to forge.

PortalAccessResponse.description:
Coverage of one managed portal in a directory read: `Outcome` is the name of an
            `Success`, `Unavailable`, `Denied`, … outcome. Anything other than `Success` means that
            portal's rows are missing from the answer — not that nobody holds a seat there.

url.description: Where it lives; may be a relative path.

PortalResponse.description: One portal the caller may open.

SetUserGroupsRequest.description:
`PUT /api/v1/admin/users/{subject}/groups`. The full set the person should hold; an empty
            array removes every seat.

rowVersion.description: Required. The base64 token from the last read of this item.

canAdminister.description: May reach administrative surfaces (operational dashboards, config).

UserCapabilitiesResponse.description:
The permission flags a client may gate its UI on, resolved server-side.
            
These are a UX affordance and NEVER a security boundary. The server authorizes every request
independently; hiding a button here protects nothing, and a caller who invokes the endpoint
directly still gets a 403. They exist so the UI can avoid offering an action that would fail —
not so the UI can decide anything.

UserGroupsResponse.description: The groups a person holds, and what a write changed.

userId.description: The identity provider's subject identifier for this caller.

displayName.description: The caller's human-readable name, for chrome that greets them.

email.description: The caller's email address; empty when the token carries none.

roles.description:
Every canonical role the caller holds — `Admin`, `Editor`, `Viewer` — never the
authorization server's raw lowercase keys, and never a role this application does not recognise.
Empty for an authenticated caller who has been issued no recognised role at all.

permissions.description:
Every `resource:action` permission the caller holds (`items:read`, `items:write`,
`admin:manage` in the shipped vocabulary). Reported next to the capability flags, never inside
Roles: a permission is not a seat.

UserProfileResponse.description:
What the CURRENT caller is and what the server will let them do — the response of
`GET /api/v1/me`, and the only place a client is told about its own permissions.
            
Every field is derived server-side from the authenticated principal. Nothing here is echoed back
from a request: a client cannot ask to be an administrator any more than it can ask to be someone
else. That is the whole point of the endpoint — the browser holds a token that says who it is,
and the server answers what that means.
